end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from where it is grown to our plate.
Identified local food as having fewer food miles.
Compared apple and spinach distances using the given locations.
Linked longer journeys with more fuel use and pollution.
Explained that strawberries may need refrigerated transport to stay fresh; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles, comparing travel distances, and connecting transport with fuel, pollution, and freshness. They used the method of checking the source and destination, and repeated the refrigerated-transport example accurately. At first, they needed prompts for the meaning of fuel and did not yet complete the full explanation of effects. At home, ask them to sort two foods into local and travelled-from-far, then explain one effect on fuel, pollution, or freshness.
